your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: My cash is $547 and the minimum next bid is $549, so I must drop out. Forcing p4 to pay $548 leaves p4 with only $124 cash and $250 in non-monopoly mortgage value ($374 max liquidity), which is well short of the $600 needed to build even 1 house per Green property before crossing my Dark Blue monopoly.

3 houses on Park Place ($1,100 rent) and Boardwalk ($1,400 rent) already exceed the total liquid net worth of every opponent (p4 maxes out at $848, p1 at $692, p3 at $209). Keeping $533 cash in reserve guarantees I can outbid any opponent (max opponent cash is $232) on unowned properties or auctions. Ending turn.

I already own 3 railroads, so Short Line doubles all four of my railroad rents from $100 to $200. Bidding $140 immediately prices out p4 ($138 cash) while keeping my cost lower in case p1 ($232) and p3 ($209) drop out rather than risk their survival cash right before Park Place and Boardwalk. If they bid higher, I have $533 and can easily outbid everyone up to $233.

Only p1 ($232 cash) remains in the auction. Owning all 4 railroads doubles rent on all four spaces from $100 to $200, which is lethal against low-cash opponents. Bidding $185 tests whether p1 will drop out before reaching their $232 cash limit while saving me money if they fold.
p1 has $232 cash. Bidding $233 prices p1 out completely and secures my fourth railroad, doubling rent to $200 across all four railroads while leaving me with $300 cash.

p1 went bankrupt to me, giving me the Light Blue monopoly (with 4 houses each) and completing my Red monopoly (Kentucky and Indiana, both mortgaged). Unmortgaging Kentucky Avenue ($121) and then Indiana Avenue ($121) activates full monopoly rent on Red and allows building on Red while still leaving me $490 cash—more than double p3 ($209) and p4 ($28) combined.
Unmortgaging Indiana Avenue for $122 completes the unmortgaged Red monopoly, enabling double rent and house building on Red while keeping $488 cash in reserve.

p3 and p4 are both on Short Line and must cross my developed Dark Blue and Light Blue monopolies next. Keeping $488 cash ensures I have more cash than p3 even if p3 passes GO ($409) and lands on Baltic Avenue, while Red is half a board away from both opponents. Ending turn.

p3 is on Community Chest (space 2) with $459 cash and no unmortgaged properties. Upgrading Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut from 4 houses to hotels for $150 total increases their rents from $320/$320/$450 to $550/$550/$600, turning every Light Blue space (rolls of 4, 6, or 7 for p3) into an instant bankruptcy while leaving me $366 cash.

With hotels now on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut Avenue, any roll of 4, 6, or 7 from Community Chest bankrupts p3 immediately. Keeping $366 cash in reserve protects against Street Repairs cards while I wait to see if p3 survives the first side of the board. Ending turn.
